caption:
Bad visa advice: "just write tourism and keep it simple."

One word under purpose of travel tells the officer nothing. A day-by-day itinerary proves three things at once: the trip is real, the budget matches the plan, and the return date is genuine.

A vague trip reads as a cover story. A specific one reads as a holiday.

slides.headline: "JUST WRITE TOURISM AND KEEP IT SIMPLE."
slides.sub: Simple is not the same as convincing.
slides.note: One word under purpose of travel tells the officer nothing they needed to know.

slides.body: Specificity is what makes a trip look real. Cities, dates, accommodation, how you move between them.
slides.note: A vague trip reads as a cover story. A specific one reads as a holiday.

slides.headline: AN ITINERARY PROVES AT ONCE
items: The trip exists as an actual plan
Your funds match what you described
The return date is genuine, not a placeholder

slides.headline: THE DETAIL THAT DECIDES IT
slides.never: Submit a rough outline with gaps in the accommodation or dates that drift from your reservations. Every gap is a question the officer has to answer without you.
slides.instead: Build the itinerary day by day, matched to the reservations and explained in the cover letter, so the file answers questions before they are asked.

slides.headline: DETAIL IS REASSURANCE.
slides.sub: It is also the cheapest thing to get right.

slides.headline: SEND ONE MESSAGE. WE DO THE REST.
